item.title: - Hermitian Adjoint of A
item.description: 1. Definition of $L : V \to V^*$ # $L : V \to V^*$, $v \mapsto \tilde{v}$, where $L(v)(w) = \tilde{v}(w) = (v \mid w)$ It’s important to note that $L$ is a conjugate-linear map. 2. Definition of $A^\dagger$ # $A^\dagger$ represents the Hermitian adjoint matrix of $A$ and is defined as follows. $$A^\dagger : V \to V, \quad A^\dagger = L^{-1} \circ A^T \circ L$$ Therefore, $A^\dagger(v) = L^{-1}(A^T(\tilde{v}))$. item.title: - Taylor Series Expansion
item.description: Introduction to Taylor Series # The Taylor series is a representation of a function as an infinite sum of terms calculated from the values of the function’s derivatives at a single point. It provides a way to approximate functions using polynomial expressions. Basic Formula # The Taylor series expansion of a function $f(x)$ around a point $x = a$ is given by: $$f(x) = \sum_{n=0}^{\infty} \frac{f^{(n)}(a)}{n!}(x-a)^n$$ Where: $f^{(n)}(a)$ represents the $n$-th derivative of $f$ evaluated at point $a$ $(x-a)$ is the distance from the expansion point Alternative Notation # If we denote $x-a = \Delta x$, the Taylor series can be written as:
